issues.summary: Metered both paid Edge Functions with a per-user daily quota (atomic consume_ai_quota RPC, fail-closed, returns 429 mapped to a friendly 'daily limit reached' message) so a free account can't loop the vision/food-search endpoints for unbounded API spend.

Made the settings persist-mutex release unconditional (plus a backoff-safe re-arm) so a mid-save edit can no longer wedge saving for the whole session — macro/goal/unit changes were silently living only in memory and vanishing on app kill.

Wrapped the nutrition-entry Delete in the shared confirmDelete dialog like every sibling flow, so one mis-tap in the options menu no longer permanently destroys the entry. Added a DevHub preview page for the confirm flow.

Added a server-side RevenueCat entitlement check (fail-closed 403, before the quota gate) to both paid Edge Functions, so premium is enforced on the server — a free account or raw curl can no longer use AI scan/macros/food search free.

Reworked Connector poison-row handling with a map-driven CONFLICT_KEYS design: permanent errors (class 22/23/42, PGRST204/205) now dead-letter instead of wedging the upload queue forever, and user_exercises natural-key conflicts self-heal instead of silently dropping the exercise.

Added a 30s abort-contract timeout, a connection-re-attempting retry, and a confirmed sign-out escape to the first-sync gate, so a fresh install with PowerSync unreachable is no longer hard-stuck on 'Syncing data…' forever.

Wired production observability: Sentry setUser + environment tag + exactly one capture per genuine failure funnel (connect, kick, disconnect-clear, sign-out failure, force-sign-out data loss, AI/foodDB edge failures, route crashes), leaving benign/expected paths uncaptured.

Persist ingredient-row quantity AND per-unit macros at full precision (they were being rounded to 1 decimal while totals used raw values), so items reconcile with the entry total and opening editEntry + tapping Save no longer silently rewrites the meal's macros.

Hardened the drifted modal twins: useSubmitOnce double-fire guards on renameModal + editEntry (no more double-write/double-pop), a try/catch on editEntry's route-param JSON.parse (crash fix), staged macro pills routed through sumItems (single owner of rounding), and the tripled workout name-check deduped into nameCheck.ts.

issues.summary: Added the project's first real CI gate (.github/workflows/ci.yml on PR/push to main): tsc typecheck blocks, jest runs advisory (continue-on-error) so an uneven suite can't block merges; added a typecheck script and switched test:ci to jest --ci. Cleared the 3 real tsc errors and corrected 4 stale test suites (incomplete connector mocks that even asserted the wrong filter column; prefs/builders pinned to abandoned plan-doc meal times vs the shipped 8:00/12:00/17:30 defaults; a graph test expecting an outcome the future-date clamp prevents), leaving the gate genuinely green (tsc 0, jest 724/724).

Wrapped the SettingsContext, WorkoutContext, and AuthContext provider value objects in useMemo (the pattern NutritionContext/BillingContext already shipped) and stabilized SettingsContext's handleGetBodyWeightProgressData with useCallback, so a settings write or token refresh no longer forces an app-wide re-render of every context consumer. Adjudication caught that WorkoutContext exposes 35 fields (not the brief's 26) and that the brief's state-values-only dep list would let userID-scoped handlers go stale during a user switch, so it used exhaustive 1:1 dep arrays; memoization-only, zero exposed values changed.

Replaced getDateKey's Intl toLocaleDateString('en-CA') with an arithmetic YYYY-MM-DD build (byte-identical: local calendar components, 4-digit year, 2-digit zero-padded month/day) — 1-2 orders of magnitude cheaper per call on the hot date-bucketing paths where a single '+' tap fired thousands of Intl calls at large log counts — and memoized the nutrition home's todayEntries so it stops re-scanning all entries every render. Output-identical everywhere (verified across ~135 call sites incl. a fixed-position slice), with equivalence/ordering/DST tests added; because the key is persisted/synced, a pre-merge on-device Hermes parity check is the one remaining human OPS step.

Consolidated the graph gap-fill day-walk that had been copy-pasted into 4 builders (macros, volume, sets, body-weight) into one shared lib/utils/graphSeries.ts buildDailySeries helper, and in the same pass fixed the live body-weight bug where days before the first weigh-in were seeded 0 — that leading 0 became values[0] in GraphStats, so the 'Change' stat reported the user's entire body weight instead of the true delta. Body-weight now carries the earliest recorded weight backward (a strict improvement); the 5 tests that pinned the 0-bug were corrected with justification and the other 3 builders' suites pass unchanged as the equivalence proof. Follow-up logged: for a >1yr user with 2+ pre-window weigh-ins the seed should be the most-recent entry <= window-start, not the earliest-ever.

issues.summary: Moved the persisted Supabase session (access JWT + long-lived refresh token) out of plaintext AsyncStorage into the iOS Keychain via a new chunked expo-secure-store adapter (native only; web keeps AsyncStorage). A required first-launch migration copies any existing plaintext session into the Keychain and deletes the plaintext, so existing users are NOT logged out on update; the adapter clears prior chunks on overwrite and writes the count last (fail-safe to a clean re-login, never a corrupt blob).

Wired real cancellation + a 30s server ceiling into the AI analyze path. Cancelling the analyze modal now aborts the in-flight fetch (an AbortController threaded from the modal through to callEdgeFunction) instead of only discarding the result client-side; the fetchOpenAI Edge Function merges the client disconnect signal with a 30s AbortSignal.timeout into both the OpenAI and Gemini fetches, normalizing an abort/timeout into the existing 504 shape to bound wall-clock/provider-cost exposure on cancel or a hung provider. Intentional cancels are filtered out of Sentry so they don't read as edge failures. (Edge Function deploy + Deno-runtime support check are OPS.)

Premise stale: the AI photo resize/compress pipeline (mealImage.ts — meal 800px/0.8, item·label 1400px/0.9, JPEG, before base64) already existed ~3 weeks before the audit, so 'photos upload full-size' was already mitigated. Added a regression guard pinning width AND exact compress AND crop-per-mode, plus an assertion that pickFromLibrary keeps allowsEditing:true (the iOS square-crop height bound) — so a future compress bump or a dropped allowsEditing can't silently reinflate the payload. No product-behavior change (mealImage.ts diff is comment-only).

Part A (memoization, zero behavior change): wrapped Graph1's chartKey and yScaleInfo in useMemo with exhaustive deps, so incidental re-renders (chart press-drag, onLayout, font churn) no longer re-run the O(n) per-point key join or the min/max+nice-step scale computation — cost that scaled with account age (up to 365 dense body-weight points at 1Y). chartKey keeps its full per-point join so interior data edits still repaint; the 200ms remount-glitch guard is untouched. Part B (reviving downsample to weekly-average the 6M/1Y body-weight line) was DEFERRED — it changes rendered output (approximate month ticks) and is a UX call.

issues.summary: Replaced uploadData's serial one-round-trip-per-op drain with a bounded-concurrency pool (MAX_CONCURRENT_UPLOAD_OPS=5) over the EXISTING single-row create/update/delete calls, so a large single writeTransaction (drag-reorder N order-bumps, bulk exercise insert, duplicate-workout) overlaps its round-trips instead of paying them serially. Perf-only: each op still issues its own single-row Supabase call with byte-identical per-op dead-letter/Sentry handling (no array batching — which the adjudication proved would introduce dup-PK/heterogeneous-key/URL-length regressions). settings + weight_progress PUT/PATCH stay strictly serial; same-id ops within a run serialize; contiguous (op,table) runs drain in order so FK order holds.

issues.summary: Added a self-rescheduling midnight setTimeout to useToday (DST-safe wall-clock next-midnight, +1s buffer) alongside the existing AppState listener, so 'today' now rolls over live at local midnight while the app stays foregrounded (streaks, week grouping, Today labels, nutrition selectedDate default) — previously only a background/foreground cycle refreshed it. Cleanup clears both the subscription and the timer. The new timer also exposed a latent test-teardown leak in DatePickerPopup.test.tsx (renders Calendar→useToday, never unmounted) — fixed by unmounting there.

Added the missing tests for the three untested persistence state machines (SettingsContext persist-save effect, the orchestrator mutex/kick throttle, the WorkoutContext order-bump store) — 14 cases across a new persistEffect.test.tsx, an extended orchestrator.test.ts, and a new WorkoutContext store test. The SettingsContext canary test revealed a REAL race and fixed it: reloadFromDisk (the rollback-on-repeated-persist-failure path) applied its async disk snapshot unconditionally, so a settings edit made mid-read was silently clobbered by the stale disk value — now guarded by an edit-sequence ref snapshotted before the read. Verified load-bearing (canary fails without the guard). A follow-up is logged for the same race in the Workout/Nutrition reloadFromDisk twins.
